description: Publish a capability (cap) to Qumge on the developer's behalf (needs the developer's Qumge key in the Authorization header). Give it a name, the API's HTTPS base_url, and — if you can read them off the project — its price book (events with a unit price) and operations (routes with a per-call ceiling, and a `doc` describing input/output so agents know what to send). It returns a DRAFT cap plus the signing secret and usage key (shown once). Nothing is charged while it is a draft. There is no human review: after test_cap passes, submit_cap takes the cap live immediately, and qumge spot-checks it afterwards (a spot check can suspend it). (Older clients may still call this tool as publish_app.)

balance_json_path.description: Only for balance_delta: where in that response.

balance_path.description: Only for balance_delta: where we read the balance.

base_url.description: Where the app lives. Must be https.

events.description: Price book events. unit_price_usd is in US dollars, e.g. 0.10.

keywords.description: Other names for the same thing, any language, up to 20. Agents search with a request like "scrape trending TikTok videos" — the keywords are what makes that find this app.

mcp_tools.description: Prices for the MCP tools you want listed. Tools you leave out are not published and are reported back to you.

name.description: Tool name, exactly as tools/list returns it.

unit_price_usd.description: Price per successful call, in USD.

mcp_url.description: Optional: publish an existing remote MCP server instead of an HTTP API. Must be https and on a domain you have verified (Profile → links). Qumge calls tools/list to discover the tools, and every tool you price with `mcp_tools` becomes one operation. Calls are billed per successful (2xx) tools/call at the price you set.

metering.description: reported (the app tells us what to charge) or balance_delta (we read its balance).

name.description: Human name shown in the store.

qumge_key.description: Optional: your Qumge API key, for clients that cannot set an Authorization header. Takes precedence over the header. Never echoed back.

refund_policy_url.description: Their refund policy, if they have one.

routes.description: HTTP routes. Billable routes need hold_usd (the most one call may cost).

doc.description: What this operation does and what it takes, for agents. Optional, but without it an agent can only guess the input shape (call_cap validates `input` against doc.input_schema).

event.description: Which price-book event this route bills. Defaults to the first event.

lane.description: standard (default: one ledger row per call) or micro — for routes priced below $0.001. A micro route must settle on_response, its per-call ceiling must be at most $0.01, and calls settle in per-minute buckets instead of one row each.

meter.description: Who counts the usage. "app" (default): your service reports after each call. "platform": Qumge counts one unit per successful (2xx) call at your declared price — use this when a call always costs the same, and you only have to write the signature check, no usage reporting.

rate_limit_per_min.description: Micro lanes only: calls per minute per key (default 600).

skill_slug.description: Optional. Attach an existing skill from the catalog to this app (its documentation then shows on the app page). Ignored if the slug is unknown.

slug.description: Optional URL slug. Derived from the name when omitted.

social_links.description: Up to 6 public URLs for the developer (X, GitHub, LinkedIn, their website). Shown on every app page. The kind is guessed from the domain.

summary.description: One line describing what it does.

support_url.description: Where users ask for help. Shown on the app page.

name: publish_cap
